footerFootnote: David Vega's personal radar. Years are counted conservatively from public writing and repositories. The chart is the open-source AOE Technology Radar.

paragraphs.headline: What the rings mean
values: The rings are years of hands-on use, not a rating of how good a technology is.
10+ years, 5+ years, and 1+ years are the buckets. The outer ring, under a year, means it has been used on a real repository, and not for a full year yet.
A quiet inner ring is intentional. Nothing is placed in 10+ years without a public record that goes back that far.

paragraphs.headline: What an entry is
values: Each entry names the projects that used the technology and says what that project is, so the link is optional.
Links point at public repositories only. Some current work is in private repositories and is described without a link.

quadrants.name: Languages and frameworks
quadrants.description: Languages and the frameworks used to build the software.

quadrants.name: Tools
quadrants.description: Editors, test runners, and the smaller programs around the code.

quadrants.name: Methods and patterns
quadrants.description: How the work is structured: testing, architecture, and documentation.

quadrants.name: Platforms and operations
quadrants.description: Where the software runs, from a laptop to a cloud cluster.

rings.name: 10+ years
rings.description: Used long enough to show up in public writing from around 2010 to 2017, and still part of the work.

rings.name: 5+ years
rings.description: Used across several years of projects. React and Kubernetes are the two that clear this bar.

rings.name: 1+ years
rings.description: Used seriously for at least a year, often on more than one project.

rings.name: < 1 year
rings.description: Tried on a real repository this past year. Promising, and too new to call a year of experience.
